slides.headline: He worked at Princeton, UCL and King's College London before coming home. In 2026, the world's math community gave him its top young-mathematician honour.
Professor Mahesh Kakde won the 2026 ICTP/IMU Ramanujan Prize for Young Mathematicians
slides.body: The $10,000 international honour, announced September 30, 2026, is jointly awarded by the Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics and the International Mathematical Union to a mathematician from a developing country - making Kakde the fifth Indian ever to win it.

slides.headline: A number theorist working on the Gross-Stark and Brumer-Stark conjectures, he held posts at Princeton, UCL and King's College London before joining IISc Bengaluru in 2019.
slides.body: His research sits in noncommutative Iwasawa theory - a corner of pure mathematics far from headlines, recognised by one of the field's most selective international prizes.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat benefits when its universities can draw talent back from Princeton and Cambridge, not just send it out.
slides.body: Kakde's career arc - India to the world's top math departments, and back to IISc - is the kind of return migration that strengthens India's research base from the inside.
